claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was Archbishop of Alexandria.
Cyril of Alexandria served as Patriarch of Alexandria from 412 to 444.
Cyril of Alexandria was born circa 376 and died in 444.
The Dialogues on the Holy and Consubstantial Trinity were addressed to Hermeias, who is described as exceedingly fond of learning and frequently inquisitive about such matters.
The work was also written for Nemesinus, described as a most learned brother.
The Dialogues were composed in seven discourses.
The discourse is in a dialogue format, proceeding by way of question and answer through two persons, with the letters α and β prefixed for each speaker.
The work was written against heretics.

The full work contains seven books covering: the Son's co-eternality and consubstantiality with the Father; the Son's being begotten according to nature; the Son as true God; the Son not being a creature; the properties of divinity in the Son; the properties of humanity pertaining to the economy with the flesh; and the Holy Spirit as God and from God according to nature.
The Greek title is Περὶ ἁγίας τε καὶ ὁμοουσίου Τριάδος (Peri hagias te kai homoousiou Triados).
A critical edition with French translation was published in three volumes by Éditions du Cerf in 1976.
